children: As the city prepares its debut five-year plan, it looks set to embrace ideas its maiden chief, Tung Chee-hwa, who has died aged 89, struggled to realise post-British rule: less reliance on property, building a tech economy and closer alignment with China's development goals.
Full view will be published shortly.
Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong’s first chief executive after its sovereignty handover to China in July 1997, died on September 8, aged 89.
John Lee, the current chief executive, will announce Hong Kong’s first Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development along with his annual policy address on September 16.
